description: Strict edits against the 61 issues that already existed before this source: 23 epics and 38 tickets. Every item carries an explicit set_fields.sprint and set_fields.status, so the pre-v2 field values are authoritative here rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan. Only the two dependency-free infra tickets remain Ready.

items.summary: Raise the test strategy to critical priority and extend it to the eleven verification categories it currently omits, so it can act as the parent of the quality epic rather than a partial statement of intent. It is an early foundations gate for the money and quality tickets that cite it.
add_acceptance_criteria: The layer table additionally covers load, stress and soak; chaos and fault injection; disaster-recovery restore drills; accessibility with a stated conformance target; performance budgets as continuous integration gates; mutation testing thresholds; automated privacy traffic inspection; billing and webhook adversarial replay; model evaluation in continuous integration; provider and consumer contract testing; and security regression smoke tests in the deploy pipeline
The strategy states the accessibility conformance target explicitly rather than describing screen-reader navigability in prose
The strategy names black-box red-team scenarios and the independent-model verification harness as deliverables with owning tickets
The Definition of Ready includes a refreshed threat model and a privacy payload review for the epic in question
Every named category maps to an owning ticket, so no category is asserted without an executable owner

The strategy publishes a numeric line-coverage floor and a numeric branch-coverage floor per named package, not one global percentage; a package with no published number is a failure of this ticket rather than an exemption
The strategy publishes a numeric mutation-score floor for every money-path package, and states that a package without a mutation floor may not carry money-path code
The strategy publishes a numeric flake quarantine rate ceiling and a numeric retry limit, and states what happens when either is exceeded
The published numbers are machine-readable, so the harnesses read them rather than restating them
The reconciliation check fails when a named package in the repository inventory has no line, branch or mutation number published for it, so an unlisted package cannot silently escape the gate
add_contracts_schema: Define the reconciliation-check contract, the backlog ticket reference format, that the strategy document and the ticket tracker both conform to, so the check can be automated rather than manually audited.
Coverage, mutation, flake and retry thresholds published as machine-readable data keyed by package name, consumed by T-QA-01, T-QA-04 and the client gates
add_security_privacy: State explicitly which categories require privacy-traffic inspection as distinct from code review, and name the tickets that produce that evidence, so docs#22's release gate has a documented source.

Require the refreshed threat model referenced in the Definition of Ready to explicitly cover the ingestion boundary, raw-content-never-leaves-device, and the parser-config signing chain, not only application-layer risks.
add_observability: Require that every category's owning ticket also states how its pass or fail signal is observed in CI or release evidence, closing the gap between naming a category and being able to verify it.
Per-package coverage, mutation score, flake rate and retry count are published each run against their floors, so a slow decline is visible before it becomes a breach
add_tests: Reconciliation check that every category named in the strategy has an owning ticket in the backlog
Automated reconciliation check additionally verifies each owning ticket reference resolves to an open or closed ticket, not a dangling identifier.
Reconciliation test that adds a package with no published number and asserts the check fails
add_rollout_rollback: Publish the strategy with a review cadence, for example at each major epic boundary, so category coverage is re-checked as new work is added rather than validated once and left stale.
add_non_goals: Implementing the harnesses, which the quality epic tickets own
Implementing the verification harnesses named in the strategy; this remains a documentation and reconciliation ticket, execution is owned by the quality epic tickets it references.

replace_text.old: | Web/admin | Playwright E2E on critical journeys only |
replace_text.new: | Web/admin | Playwright E2E on critical journeys, plus accessibility conformance and performance budgets as CI gates |

replace_text.old: - [ ] Coverage expectations: high bar on money paths, pragmatic elsewhere
replace_text.new: - [ ] Coverage expectations: high bar on money paths, pragmatic elsewhere, with a mutation-testing threshold enforced in CI on ledger, debt, budget and split packages

items.set_outcome: Every verification category named in the published strategy maps to a specific owning ticket in the backlog, confirmed by a reconciliation check that fails the build if any category is left unowned.
items.set_parallel_boundary: The reconciliation check and category-to-ticket mapping can be authored and validated independent of any quality-epic ticket being started, since it only requires ticket references to exist, not their work to be complete.
add_scope: Define a test taxonomy that tells each change class when unit, property, integration, contract, end-to-end, security and manual evidence are mandatory.
Publish a shared synthetic-fixture ownership model so repositories reuse governed builders and golden cases rather than inventing incompatible test data.
Define evidence retention and naming rules so a release checklist can consume current results without relying on links to expired CI artifacts.
add_definition_of_done: The reconciliation check runs against the current backlog state and passes with zero unowned categories before this ticket closes.
The accessibility conformance target's specific standard and level are confirmed present in the published document, not only referenced as a goal.

items.summary: Extend the release and threat-model documentation to cite the evidence produced by the platform, privacy-capture and governance tickets. The penetration test and red-team execution ticket consumes this document, so it is not listed as a prerequisite of it.
add_acceptance_criteria: Every gate has a named owner recorded in the checklist rather than an assertion that owners exist
Backup restore has been verified and its timing is attached to the release record
Rollback has been rehearsed per component and the evidence is attached, not merely planned
Service level objectives and alerting are live and at least one alert has been proven to reach the on-call owner
The cross-tenant, request-forgery and numeric-provenance suites are green for the release candidate
The audit chain verification job is green
Accessibility and performance budget gates are green
The data safety declaration has been re-checked against traffic captured for this release candidate
Independent second-reviewer approval is recorded for the release
add_contracts_schema: Define the release-evidence-record schema, gate name, owner, evidence link, timestamp, waiver if any, as a structured artifact attached to each release, rather than a checklist of prose checkboxes.
add_security_privacy: Require the data-safety re-check to reference the specific traffic capture used as evidence for that release candidate, not a prior release's capture, closing a gap where stale evidence could be reused unnoticed.
Require the waiver-expiry test to also check that an expired waiver from a prior release cannot be silently carried forward into the current release-evidence record.
add_observability: Require the alert-to-on-call proof to include a timestamp and the specific on-call owner who acknowledged it, making the evidence auditable rather than a bare assertion.
add_tests: A release-candidate rehearsal fails when any required evidence artifact is absent and passes only when the complete evidence set is attached
A waiver-expiry test proves an expired gate waiver cannot authorize a release
Cross-reference test verifying every gate listed in the checklist has a corresponding evidence-producing ticket reference, mirroring docs#21's reconciliation check.
add_rollout_rollback: A gate may be waived only in writing, with a named approver and an expiry date, and the waiver is attached to the release record

Rehearse the full release-candidate evidence assembly at least once per quarter even without an imminent release, so the process is proven working under no time pressure before it is needed under deadline pressure.
add_non_goals: Defining the individual gate implementations, the audit-chain job, the cross-tenant suite, accessibility conformance; this ticket owns the checklist and evidence contract, not the underlying verification code.

replace_text.old: - [ ] Rollback plan documented per component
replace_text.new: - [ ] Rollback rehearsed per component with the evidence attached, not merely documented

replace_text.old: - docs#21 (test strategy), T-QA-10 (penetration test and remediation gate), T-QA-09 (automated privacy traffic inspection), T-PLT-02 (restore drill), T-GOV-03 (independent second reviewer)
replace_text.new: - docs#21 (test strategy)

items.set_outcome: A release-candidate rehearsal fails when the audit-chain verification job, the cross-tenant suite, or an accessibility gate is missing evidence, and passes only once every named gate's evidence is attached.
items.set_parallel_boundary: The release-evidence-record schema and waiver-record format can be authored independent of docs#21 reaching completion, since both documents can be drafted in parallel and reconciled at review; the cross-reference test is gated on docs#21's category-to-ticket mapping existing first.
add_scope: Name a specific owner role, not only a person, for each gate category so ownership survives personnel changes without a document update.
Define the environment-promotion order and the minimum evidence required to move a release candidate from development to staging and from staging to production.

Cross-reference each privacy and security gate to the specific ticket that produces its evidence, docs#21's test strategy, the privacy-traffic inspection ticket, the independent-review ticket, so the checklist is traceable rather than aspirational.
add_definition_of_done: The release-evidence-record schema is published and at least one rehearsal run demonstrates a missing-evidence failure and a complete-evidence pass, as already required by add_tests.
The cross-reference test passes with zero gates lacking an evidence-producing ticket.

items.summary: The activation instrumentation ticket assumes an analytics platform nobody has been asked to build and an SDK position nobody has reconciled with the message permission commitment.
add_acceptance_criteria: The analytics destination is provisioned and its region is recorded before any event is emitted
An inventory of every embedded third-party component is recorded and referenced by the data safety declaration
Error reporting scrubbing is verified with a planted monetary value rather than assumed
The event payload allowlist is a shared artifact consumed by both Android and web, so the two cannot drift
No analytics event fires before the analytics purpose has been consented
The funnel and cohort instrumentation this ticket lands is the measurement T-RET-01 reports its holdout comparison against; a retention metric with no instrumented source fails review
add_contracts_schema: The shared event-payload allowlist is published as a versioned schema artifact consumed by both android and web build pipelines, so a key added on one platform without the other is a detectable schema mismatch, not a silent drift
add_security_privacy: No embedded component may observe message-derived data; this is verified by traffic capture rather than by code review
The consent-state machine defaults to not-consented on first launch and on any app update, requiring an explicit affirmative action before the first event of any kind is queued for send
add_observability: Consent-state transition counts (granted, revoked) are themselves tracked as a privacy-safe meta-metric, so a sudden spike in revocations after a release is visible as a signal worth investigating
add_tests: Traffic capture assertion that no analytics payload contains a monetary value or message content
Opt-out test proving zero outbound analytics calls after the toggle
A CI test runs the payload-allowlist linter against a deliberately planted disallowed key and confirms the build fails
A funnel-drop-off test seeds a simulated cohort with abandonment at each step and asserts the report attributes drop-off to the correct step
add_rollout_rollback: The consent-state machine ships with a kill switch that, if flipped, stops all event emission immediately regardless of any individual user's prior consent state, for use if a payload leak is discovered post-release
add_non_goals: Building a general-purpose analytics platform for future non-activation events; this ticket instruments the stated funnel and engagement events only
Attributing retention differences to specific marketing channels; acquisition-channel attribution is out of scope
items.set_outcome: A privacy reviewer can capture live outbound analytics traffic for a full session covering every instrumented event and confirm zero fields carry a monetary value, a balance, or any message-derived content.
items.set_parallel_boundary: Instrumentation call sites can be added to each screen as it ships as long as every new event key is added to the shared allowlist schema first; the funnel dashboard itself depends on the analytics destination being provisioned, which blocks only the reporting layer, not event capture.
add_scope: A consent-state machine (not yet consented, granted, revoked) with a single source of truth checked before every event emission call site, rather than each call site checking a boolean independently

A funnel-drop-off report distinguishing where in install-to-payoff-date-viewed users abandon, so a retention problem can be localised to a specific step rather than only observed in aggregate weekly numbers
A payload-allowlist linter running in CI that fails the build if an event call site references a property key not present in the shared allowlist artifact
add_definition_of_done: The payload-allowlist linter is demonstrated failing on a planted violation in CI, not only passing on clean code
The consent kill switch has been exercised in a test environment and confirmed to stop event emission within one app session

items.summary: Pin the Android skeleton to the canonical stack so later tickets are not written against an undecided architecture, and record the deferrals explicitly. The buildable scaffold and the generated client contract are the real prerequisites; feature architecture, encrypted storage and navigation stay in this ticket.
add_acceptance_criteria: The skeleton uses the canonical declarative user interface, unidirectional state, dependency injection, encrypted local database, typed HTTP client and background work stack
The deferred sync engine and query-generation library are recorded as deferred with the reason, so no later ticket assumes them
The build runs lint, unit tests and instrumented tests through the shared workflow and fails on a planted violation
The local database is encrypted from the first commit rather than retrofitted
Crash symbolication works with code shrinking enabled
The skeleton builds on top of the delivered android scaffold rather than re-creating the Gradle, lint and unit test setup
The generated API client is consumed from the published contract package rather than hand-written
add_contracts_schema: The generated Ktor client module is published as a versioned internal artifact with its own changelog entry per contracts release, so a screen's minimum supported client version is traceable
add_security_privacy: The Android Keystore-backed encryption key for the Room database is generated per install and never exported, logged or transmitted, verified by a test that attempts to read the raw database file and confirms it is unreadable without the key
add_observability: Build health (lint violations, test pass rate, shrink-and-symbolicate success) is tracked per merged commit on the shared workflow dashboard, so a regression in the scaffold itself is visible before it blocks a feature ticket
add_tests: A static-analysis test asserting the Double-forbidden-in-money-types rule fires on a deliberately planted violation, proving the rule is enforced rather than merely documented
An instrumented test confirms the Room database file is unreadable when opened without the Keystore-derived key, on both target API levels
add_rollout_rollback: The scaffold ships to no end user directly; a defect surfaces as a failed shared-workflow gate on a dependent ticket, and the fix is a scaffold patch release consumed by re-running that ticket's CI
add_non_goals: Adopting an offline sync vendor, which is settled by the sync contract ticket
Implementing any feature screen; this ticket delivers only the architecture, build and enforcement scaffolding those screens will build on
Choosing or wiring a feature-flag or remote-config system; that decision is deferred alongside the sync engine
items.set_outcome: A new screen added to the skeleton can only reach the network through the generated Ktor client, is exercised by an instrumented test on both target emulators, and cannot compile if it references a floating-point type in a money-typed field.
items.set_parallel_boundary: Feature screens cannot start against the generated client until this ticket publishes the network-module boundary; the accessibility and Double-forbidden lint rules apply to every screen ticket from the moment they merge.
add_scope: A static-analysis custom rule forbidding Double or Float in any class or function named or annotated as money, enforced in the shared CI workflow rather than by convention
A minimal accessibility baseline (a required content-description lint check and a default TalkBack smoke test) wired into the same instrumented test scaffold so every later screen inherits it
A network-module boundary that fails the build if any file outside the generated-client package issues a raw HTTP call, enforced by a dependency-rule check rather than code review alone
add_definition_of_done: The Double-forbidden lint rule is demonstrated against a planted violation in a throwaway branch and shown to fail the build
The Keystore-backed encryption test passes on both target emulators (API 31 and current)

items.summary: The contract skeleton currently types money in a way generated TypeScript clients cannot represent safely; it must adopt the money, time and idempotency conventions before any client is generated from it.
add_acceptance_criteria: Monetary amounts use the exact JSON representation accepted by T-ADR-MONEY-01; generated clients expose a domain wrapper and never an unsafe raw 64-bit JSON number or floating-point number
Generated Kotlin and TypeScript clients round-trip every amount without loss, proven by a cross-language test over generated values
Instants are represented in a single documented format and the calendar time zone is carried separately where it matters
Every financial write operation declares an idempotency key with its scope and lifetime
Generation is deterministic and re-running it on an unchanged specification produces identical output
The specification is published from the scaffolded contracts repository through its own lint, generate and publish pipeline
The TypeScript client exposes the domain wrapper accepted by T-ADR-MONEY-01; no generated surface exposes an unsafe raw 64-bit JSON number or a bigint across a JSON or React Server Component boundary
Kotlin, TypeScript and Python clients are all generated and published from this specification; a target language that is skipped fails the pipeline rather than being silently absent

The generated Python client represents money as a Decimal-backed wrapper carrying its currency, never as a float or a bare int, and a cross-language round-trip test covers Kotlin, TypeScript and Python together
add_contracts_schema: Money, instant and idempotency key components defined once and referenced everywhere rather than repeated per endpoint
A pagination envelope schema (cursor, page_size, has_more) defined once for list endpoints; every monetary field remains conditional on the wire representation accepted by T-ADR-MONEY-01.
A version and deprecation policy covering compatibility windows, sunset signalling and generated-client support for additive and breaking contract changes.

Generator configuration names three first-class targets - Kotlin, TypeScript and Python - each with a pinned generator version, because the ai-service is a Python consumer of this contract and not an exception to it
add_security_privacy: The specification declares the bearer-token authentication scheme at the root level so no endpoint can be generated without an explicit security requirement, closing the gap where an endpoint silently defaults to public.
add_observability: The client-generation pipeline publishes a build artifact recording the specification hash it generated from, so a mismatch between a deployed client and the current specification is detectable from the artifact metadata alone.
add_tests: Cross-language round-trip test over generated amounts including the maximum representable value
Contract test asserting no endpoint accepts a bare numeric amount
Registry-completeness test asserting every currency code accepted by the specification has a matching exponent entry in the api#1 currency registry, failing when the two lists diverge.
Contract tests for pagination boundaries, unsupported filters, unstable sort attempts and expired API versions.
Python client generation, import and type-check test in a smoke consumer project
add_rollout_rollback: Publish regenerated Kotlin and TypeScript clients to a prerelease artifact channel for an initial rollout window before promoting them to the default consumed version, and roll back by pinning consuming repositories to the prior published client version if a generated client fails its round-trip test after promotion.
add_non_goals: Generating a client in any language beyond Kotlin and TypeScript for this contract release.

replace_text.old: **Money is always modelled as an object**: `{ amount_minor: integer(int64), currency: string }`
replace_text.new: **Money follows the accepted T-ADR-MONEY-01 wire representation**

replace_text.old: Model errors as RFC 7807 problem+json for consistency.
replace_text.new: Model errors as RFC 9457 application/problem+json for consistency.

items.set_outcome: A change to the money, instant or idempotency-key schema component in the OpenAPI specification regenerates identical Kotlin and TypeScript client code on every run, so a specification change and its generated clients never drift silently between commits.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns the contracts repository's specification, schema components and generated-client publishing pipeline; the api repository consumes the published clients for its contract tests and never redefines the money, instant or idempotency-key shapes locally.
add_scope: A published problem+json error catalogue enumerating the specific error codes this ticket introduces, so clients branch on a stable identifier rather than parsing a message string.
A versioned changelog entry format recording which schema components changed in each contract release, distinct from general CHANGELOG.md prose.
A contract-only example fixture set, one valid and one invalid payload per endpoint, that api#3's contract-test harness consumes directly instead of authoring its own fixtures.
Shared cursor-pagination, filter and sort conventions with explicit limits, stable ordering and invalid-query error codes.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer confirms the generated TypeScript client's public money type matches the accepted T-ADR-MONEY-01 wire representation before any client is marked consumable.

items.summary: The money primitive must implement the published wire conventions rather than an internal-only representation, so the ban on floating point is enforced at the boundary as well as in the domain.
add_acceptance_criteria: The primitive serialises to and from the exact wire representation accepted by T-ADR-MONEY-01 with its currency
Mixing currencies in an arithmetic operation is a compile-time or immediate runtime failure rather than a silent coercion
The continuous integration check rejects floating point money in serialisation code as well as in domain code
Round-trip conversion is verified against the generated clients rather than only within the backend
add_contracts_schema: A currency-exponent registry entry format (code, exponent, minor_unit_name) shared between contracts#1 and api#1 so the two repositories read the same exponent data instead of each hardcoding it.
add_security_privacy: Money values never appear in logs at any precision; diagnostics use operation identifiers and field names without amounts or account data.
add_observability: A build-time metric counting how many source files the floating-point money guard scanned, so a silent narrowing of the guard's scope shows up as a drop in that count.
add_tests: Property test over generated amounts asserting round-trip stability through the wire format
Negative test proving a mixed-currency operation fails
Registry-completeness test asserting every currency code accepted by the contracts specification has a matching exponent entry in the api#1 registry, failing when the two diverge.
add_rollout_rollback: Introduce the floating-point CI guard in warn-only mode against the existing codebase first to catch pre-existing violations before flipping it to a hard failure, and roll back to warn-only if the initial hard-failure run blocks an unrelated, already-merged change.
add_non_goals: Implementing currency conversion or exchange-rate lookup, which remains the responsibility of the transfer and reporting tickets that consume this primitive.

replace_text.old: Serialisation matches the contract shape `{ amount_minor, currency }`
replace_text.new: Serialisation matches the wire representation accepted by T-ADR-MONEY-01

items.set_outcome: Adding a new financial field typed as Double, Float or BigDecimal anywhere in the api repository fails the build immediately and identifies the offending file, before the change can reach pull request review.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns the Money value type and its CI floating-point guard inside the api repository; the contracts repository owns the wire shape accepted by T-ADR-MONEY-01, and neither ticket redefines the other's representation.
add_scope: A currency-exponent registry mapping each supported ISO-4217 code to its decimal exponent, sourced from shared data rather than scattered per-currency conditionals.
A conversion function from the internal minor-units representation to the wire format accepted by T-ADR-MONEY-01, exercised by every serialisation path.
A lint rule that flags a raw arithmetic operator used directly on two Money values instead of the value type's own operators.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer confirms the primitive's serialised output for a maximum-magnitude amount matches the accepted T-ADR-MONEY-01 wire representation before this ticket is marked done.

items.summary: The ledger schema must be written so it can carry the encryption and multi-currency decisions without a later rewrite: amounts stay constrained integers, and the currency and clearing structures are reserved now.
add_acceptance_criteria: The zero-sum constraint is expressed per currency so it remains valid when multi-currency arrives
Every transaction is single-currency in the minimum viable product and the schema makes a mixed-currency transaction impossible to insert
Amount columns are integer columns protected by row-level security and storage encryption rather than application-layer ciphertext
Clearing account and linked exchange group structures are reserved without being populated
Forced row-level security is enabled on every tenant-scoped table from the first migration

This ticket enables FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and a default-deny policy on every tenant-scoped table; the low-privilege application role, the write checks, the invoker-rights functions and the grant-mediating predicate are T-SEC-01's and are explicitly not delivered here
add_contracts_schema: A reversing-transaction linkage schema (original_transaction_id, reversal_transaction_id, reason) recorded at the database level so a correction is traceable without scanning free-text descriptions.
add_security_privacy: The schema records which columns are constrained, which are encrypted and which are blind-indexed, matching the encryption decision record

The application's runtime database role has no UPDATE or DELETE grant on the entries table, verified by attempting both operations with that role's own credentials and confirming Postgres rejects them.
add_observability: A scheduled reconciliation query comparing the derived balance from entries against any cached downstream read-model balance, alerting on any divergence above zero.
add_tests: Direct insert test proving an unbalanced entry set is rejected by the database
Direct insert test proving a mixed-currency transaction is rejected
Privilege test connecting as the restricted application role and asserting both an UPDATE and a DELETE against entries are rejected by Postgres.
add_rollout_rollback: Apply the append-only role restriction after verifying the migration role's own path still succeeds in staging, and roll back to the prior broader role only if a legitimate operational need for runtime UPDATE access is found, which would itself signal a design defect to fix rather than a permanent rollback.
add_non_goals: Implementing the reversing-transaction business logic for edits and deletes at the application layer, which api#7 owns; this ticket provides only the schema-level linkage.

The low-privilege database role, row-level write checks, invoker-rights functions and the grant-mediated cross-user read predicate, all of which T-SEC-01 owns; this ticket owns FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and default deny only
The migration runner and registry, which T-MIG-01 owns; this ticket supplies migrations that the runner applies
items.set_outcome: An attempt to run UPDATE or DELETE against the entries table using the application's runtime database role is rejected by Postgres privileges directly, not merely discouraged by application-layer convention.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns the ledger schema, its database-enforced invariants and role privileges inside the api repository; downstream tickets such as api#7 and api#9 consume this schema and do not alter its constraints.
add_scope: A database role definition that excludes UPDATE and DELETE grants on the entries table for the runtime connection, separate from the migration role used only during deploys.
A reversing-transaction helper that creates a correction referencing the original transaction id, so every caller produces reversals the same way.
An index review note naming the specific composite indexes added for entries-by-account and transactions-by-user-and-date-range, with the query pattern each one serves.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer connects as the restricted application database role and confirms an UPDATE or DELETE against entries is rejected before this ticket is marked done.

items.summary: The test harness ticket should establish the hooks that the money-path verification gates plug into, rather than only property-based and contract testing.
add_acceptance_criteria: The harness exposes a shared generator module that the money-path invariant suites reuse rather than duplicating
The harness is structured so mutation testing and independent-model comparison can be added as gates without restructuring
Failure output prints the minimal reproducing case rather than full records
add_contracts_schema: A shared fixture schema (input, expected_invariant, tolerance) referenced by both the property-based generators and the contract tests, so a fixture is never duplicated in two formats.
add_security_privacy: No test fixture or generator seed contains real user data or a real financial institution's export format, satisfied by using synthetic Indian-format data throughout.
add_observability: Test suite output records wall-clock duration per test category, property, contract and integration, so a regression toward the existing 5-minute budget is attributable to a specific category.
add_tests: Self-test proving the harness fails when an invariant is deliberately violated
Flaky-test detection test that runs a deliberately non-deterministic fixture repeatedly and confirms the quarantine mechanism flags it.
add_rollout_rollback: Introduce the flaky-test quarantine mechanism as advisory logging before it is allowed to skip a test automatically, and roll back to advisory-only if quarantining is found to suppress a genuine regression during that trial.
add_non_goals: Building the independent-model comparison harness itself, which remains a separately owned quality-epic ticket that only reuses this harness's structure.
items.set_outcome: Running the full test suite locally and in CI produces the same pass or fail result for every test, with no test that passes only in isolation or only in one environment.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns the shared test-harness infrastructure and generator modules inside the api repository; feature tickets such as api#2 and api#7 write their own invariant tests against this harness rather than modifying the harness itself.
add_scope: A documented seed-corpus format for property-based generators so the awkward-value seeds are versioned and reusable rather than embedded ad hoc in each test file.

A CI stage that runs contract tests against the currently generated client artifacts from contracts#1, separate from the property-based test stage, so the two failure classes are distinguishable in CI output.
A flaky-test quarantine mechanism that flags a test unreliable after a defined number of non-deterministic failures, distinct from silently retrying it.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer confirms the shared generator module is imported by at least one ledger invariant test and one non-ledger test, proving it is genuinely shared rather than nominally shared.

items.summary: Registration and login must not become Ready until the authentication decision record closes, and must emit audit events and support phone verification from the start.
add_acceptance_criteria: Passkey support is either implemented or explicitly deferred in line with the authentication decision record, with no silent divergence from the security checklist
Phone number verification is available and its hashed result is usable by the trial anti-abuse control
Every authentication outcome writes an audit event through the shared audit service
Responses do not reveal whether an account exists
The relying-party identifier and origin set match the decision record exactly
Authentication is implemented only after the shared audit event service exists; no local or temporary audit table is introduced
add_contracts_schema: An auth-event schema (event_type, account_id_or_null, outcome, client_ip_hash, timestamp) published once so every authentication outcome writes a structurally identical audit record regardless of code path.
add_security_privacy: Phone numbers are stored hashed with a per-deployment salt and never in the clear

Failed-login rate limiting is keyed on a hashed identifier rather than the raw email or phone number, so the rate-limit store itself does not become a new place personal identifiers are held in the clear.
add_observability: An alert on a sustained spike in failed-login rate-limit triggers within a short rolling window, distinguishing a credential-stuffing attempt from ordinary user error.
add_tests: Account enumeration attempt test
Audit event emission test for every authentication outcome
Breached-password rejection test asserting a password present on the breached list is refused at registration.
add_rollout_rollback: Roll out account lockout with exponential backoff behind a feature flag defaulting to a conservative threshold, and treat disabling lockout as an incident-response measure only, never a permanent posture, since lockout is a core control rather than an optional enhancement.
add_non_goals: Choosing the recovery mechanism, relying-party identifier or device-binding policy, which T-ADR-AUTH-05 owns.
items.set_outcome: A login attempt against a locked-out account returns the identical response shape and comparable timing to a login attempt with merely a wrong password, so no client-observable signal distinguishes lockout from an ordinary failed attempt.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns registration, login, lockout and audit emission inside the api repository; the web and admin repositories consume the resulting tokens and implement no password or lockout logic of their own.
add_scope: A documented password-hash migration path for rotating the Argon2id cost parameters later without forcing an immediate mass password reset.
A breached-password list refresh mechanism with a stated update cadence, so the check does not silently run against a stale list indefinitely.
Authentication implementation consumes the recovery, passkey, relying-party and device-binding model accepted in T-ADR-AUTH-05; no ticket-local fallback policy is invented.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer attempts five rapid failed logins against a test account and confirms both the lockout response and the audit trail record the attempt without revealing whether the account exists.

items.summary: Refresh token rotation must follow the authentication decision record and write audit events, because reuse detection is a security event that has to be attributable.
add_acceptance_criteria: Whether refresh tokens are device-bound follows the authentication decision record rather than being chosen during implementation
A detected reuse revokes the whole token family and writes an audit event
The client is told why it was signed out in a way that does not disclose token internals
add_contracts_schema: A token-family record schema (family_id, device_id, created_at, revoked_at, revocation_reason) so reuse detection and the eventual session-listing feature read the same structure.
add_security_privacy: Revoked refresh tokens remain in storage only as a hash with a revocation timestamp, never as recoverable plaintext, consistent with the existing rule against storing raw refresh tokens.
add_observability: A dashboard counter for token-family revocations attributable to reuse detection, separate from revocations caused by absolute session expiry, so a spike in reuse-triggered revocations is distinguishable from routine expiry.
add_tests: Reuse detection test asserting family revocation and audit emission
Grace-window boundary test asserting a refresh arriving exactly at the edge of the configured window is treated consistently rather than by chance.
add_rollout_rollback: Deploy reuse detection with revocation logging only, before enabling actual family revocation, so the false-positive rate from the grace window can be measured against real traffic; rollback is reverting to logging-only if the measured false-positive rate exceeds an acceptable threshold.
add_non_goals: Building a user-facing session-management screen that lists or revokes individual devices, which belongs to a client-side feature ticket.
items.set_outcome: Replaying a refresh token that has already been rotated once immediately invalidates every other active session in the same login family, and a subsequent request from any of those sessions is rejected within the same request cycle.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns refresh-token rotation and family revocation logic inside the api repository; client repositories, android, web and admin, only handle the resulting sign-out response and implement no rotation logic themselves.
add_scope: A documented grace-window duration for the near-simultaneous refresh race case, stated as a concrete value rather than left to implementation discretion.
A per-family session listing suitable for an eventual sign-out-all-devices feature, showing how many active sessions exist in a token family.
A metrics counter distinguishing legitimate concurrent refreshes resolved by the grace window from genuine reuse-triggered revocations.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer fires two concurrent refresh requests from the same simulated client and confirms neither a false revocation nor a duplicate token family results, using the documented grace window.

items.summary: Transaction creation is a financial write and must carry idempotency and audit semantics from the start rather than acquiring them later.
add_acceptance_criteria: Creation requires an idempotency key and a replayed request returns the original result without creating a second transaction
Concurrent creation with the same key produces exactly one transaction, proven by a race test
A rejected creation leaves no partial entries
add_contracts_schema: An idempotency record schema linking the accepted key representation, request fingerprint and transaction identifier exactly as T-ADR-MONEY-01 specifies.
add_security_privacy: Idempotency keys are scoped per authenticated user, so one user's key cannot be replayed against another user's session to read or duplicate their transaction.
add_observability: A metric for idempotency-key collisions where the same key was submitted with a different request body, since a nonzero rate indicates a client bug generating keys incorrectly.
add_tests: Idempotency replay test
Concurrent same-key race test
Conformance tests cover replay and conflicting key reuse using the exact response semantics accepted in T-ADR-MONEY-01.
add_rollout_rollback: Ship the idempotency implementation only after T-ADR-MONEY-01 is accepted; rollback disables new transaction writes while preserving every recorded key and ledger effect for safe replay.
add_non_goals: Implementing recurring or scheduled transaction creation, which is a separate feature outside this ticket's scope.
items.set_outcome: Two requests carrying different idempotency keys but otherwise identical transaction content are treated as two independent transactions, confirming the idempotency key alone, not the payload, determines duplication.
items.set_context: Transaction creation is the first user-controlled write into the append-only ledger. It must bind the public request shape, idempotency record and balanced-entry transaction into one atomic boundary, because any locally invented retry or correction rule would create duplicate money or partial ledger effects.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns transaction creation, editing and deletion semantics inside the api repository; the categories ticket api#9 and the transfer ticket api#8 both build on this ticket's transaction shape rather than redefining it.
add_scope: Idempotency storage implements the scope, lifetime and conflict behaviour accepted in T-ADR-MONEY-01, with no ticket-local default.
A response field marking the idempotency-replay case as replayed rather than freshly created, so clients distinguish the two without inferring it from timestamps.
A correcting-entry linkage exposed in the transaction read model so an edited or deleted transaction's correction chain is visible to a client rather than only reconstructable from raw ledger rows.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer submits the same idempotency key twice with different request bodies and confirms the second request is rejected rather than returning the first result.

items.summary: Categories must be implemented as the append-only reporting dimension the decision record specifies, including splits, merge redirects and cycle prevention.
add_acceptance_criteria: Categories are a reporting dimension and are not modelled as ledger accounts
A transaction can be split across several categories and the allocation must sum exactly to the transaction amount
Merging a category creates a redirect rather than rewriting history, and the redirect depth is bounded
A merge that would create a cycle is rejected
Historical reporting follows the as-of semantics chosen in the decision record
add_contracts_schema: A category-split schema (transaction_id, category_id, amount) distinct from the single-category assignment case, published so contracts#1's transaction endpoints can represent both shapes without ambiguity.
add_security_privacy: No new security or privacy control is introduced by category management beyond existing transaction-level access control, since categories carry no sensitive data of their own.
add_observability: A count of category-merge operations per week and their average redirect chain length, so an unexpectedly deep or frequent merge pattern is visible before it affects report performance.
add_tests: Split allocation sum constraint test
Merge cycle rejection test
As-of reporting test across a merge boundary
Archive-in-use test asserting a category with assigned transactions can be archived without being blocked, distinct from the delete-blocked case.
add_definition_of_done: The category schema and report queries are reviewed against T-ADR-CAT-02
A category merge is proven not to rewrite historical ledger entries
A reviewer creates a split transaction whose allocations sum to one unit less than the transaction total and confirms the API rejects it with an error naming the shortfall amount.
add_rollout_rollback: Introduce category splits as an additive schema change alongside the existing single-category assignment, so existing single-category transactions require no migration; release the split feature only after the sum-validation test passes in staging, since no rollback path removes splits once a transaction has used them.
add_non_goals: Supporting shared or team-wide custom categories across multiple users, which is out of scope for the single-user category model this ticket defines.
items.set_outcome: Deleting or attempting to delete a category that has at least one transaction assigned to it is rejected by the API with a message offering merge or archive, and the transaction's category assignment is left unchanged.
items.set_context: Categories are a reporting dimension over immutable ledger history, not bookkeeping accounts and not mutable labels that may silently rewrite old reports. The model must support defaults, user-defined values, splits and merges while preserving as-of reporting and one contract shared by every client.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns category definition, splits and merge semantics inside the api repository; reporting and budget tickets in later epics read categories through this ticket's schema and define no category storage of their own.
add_scope: A default category seed list reviewed against real Indian spending categories beyond the examples already named, published as a versioned data file rather than inline code.
An icon and colour value registry with a fixed enumerated set, so client applications do not need to handle arbitrary free-form values.
A split-allocation validation error format naming the exact shortfall or excess amount when a split does not sum to the transaction total, rather than a generic rejection.

items.summary: Statement import must be idempotent and preview-first, because a duplicated import of months of history is both a data problem and a trust problem.
add_acceptance_criteria: A dry run writes nothing and its preview lists creates, updates, duplicates and rejects
Re-importing the same file creates no duplicates, proven by a test
A malformed row is reported with its position and reason and does not abort the whole import
A cancelled or failed import leaves no partially committed records

The preview, commit, column-mapping, error, confidence and dedup-outcome payloads are the shared components published by T-CON-10; this ticket defines no import schema of its own and a locally declared shape fails contract verification
add_contracts_schema: Uses the T-CON-10 import components verbatim - import preview, commit result, column mapping, row error, confidence band and dedup outcome - so the Android and web import screens render one shape rather than one per client
add_security_privacy: Uploaded statement files are deleted from temporary storage once the import is committed or cancelled, so a bank statement is never retained longer than the import workflow requires.
add_observability: A per-import metric recording rows created, duplicates skipped and rows rejected, so an institution whose mapping preset silently degrades produces a visible shift in these ratios over time.
add_tests: Idempotent re-import test
Partial failure isolation test
Fuzzy-duplicate confidence test asserting a near-match row is flagged with a lower confidence than an exact-match duplicate rather than being treated identically.
add_rollout_rollback: Launch import for the initially verified Indian bank formats first, expanding the supported-format registry incrementally, and roll back a specific institution's mapping preset independently if it is found to misparse a real export, without disabling import for other institutions.
add_non_goals: Automated ongoing bank-statement fetching or scheduled polling, which is out of scope for this manual upload and preview feature.
items.set_outcome: Uploading the same bank statement file a second time after a successful import produces a dry-run preview showing every row as a duplicate, with zero rows marked as creates, before any commit step runs.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns CSV and statement import, its dry-run preview and duplicate detection inside the api repository; the automated SMS-capture epic owns its own duplicate matcher and shares only the fuzzy-matching approach by convention, not shared code ownership here.
add_scope: A mapping-preset versioning scheme so an institution's column mapping can be corrected later without silently reinterpreting already-imported historical files.
A confidence indicator on each detected duplicate in the dry-run preview, distinguishing an exact match from a fuzzy match so a user can review uncertain cases before committing.
A supported-bank-format registry listing which Indian bank export shapes have a verified mapping preset, distinct from the generic column-mapping fallback.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer uploads the same verified bank export file twice and confirms the second dry-run preview shows every row as a duplicate before any commit action is available.

items.summary: Debt modelling must follow the ledger decision record: balances derive from liability entries and lender statements are reconciliation snapshots rather than an authoritative current balance.
add_acceptance_criteria: No stored current balance is treated as authoritative; balances derive from liability account entries
A lender statement is recorded as a timestamped reconciliation snapshot with its own identity
A discrepancy between a statement and the derived balance is recorded as an explicit ledger adjustment rather than an in-place correction
The model supports fixed and variable rate debts, fees and minimum payment rules without a client-side special case
add_contracts_schema: MinorUnitAmount and BasisPointsRate become named schema types that map the accepted wire representation to integer domain wrappers without exposing raw primitives
StatementSnapshot resource schema carries a capturedAt timestamp, a source field (manual or imported) and a reference id to the ledger adjustment it produced
DebtType enum is published as a versioned schema component so a ninth debt type requires a schema version bump rather than a silent server-side string addition
add_security_privacy: Statement snapshot storage excludes any lender login credential or authentication token, consistent with the no-account-aggregator non-goal already stated
APR and balance values never appear in request, response or debug logs because the pair can identify the exact loan product a user holds
add_observability: A daily count of reconciliation adjustments is emitted split by debit or credit direction, so a spike after a schema or parsing change is visible before a support ticket arrives
Debt creation emits a structured event carrying only debt type and rate convention, with no monetary field, so type mix over time is visible without exposing amounts
add_tests: Reconciliation discrepancy adjustment test
Derived balance equivalence test after a sequence of adjustments
Contract test asserting the generated client's APR and balance fields deserialize as integers, failing the build if a future edit reintroduces a decimal or float type
Round trip test creating a debt through the API and reading it back through the generated client, asserting the minor-unit amount and basis-point rate are bit for bit identical
add_rollout_rollback: Debt and reconciliation-adjustment tables ship as additive migrations; disabling the reconciliation endpoint on rollback leaves every already-recorded adjustment untouched
The DebtType schema version is checked at debt-creation time so a client on an older schema version cannot submit a type the server does not yet recognise
add_non_goals: Parsing or importing a statement file automatically; this ticket defines only where a snapshot is stored once captured by any means
Backfilling debts created before this schema existed onto the derived-balance rule; that migration is a separate piece of work
items.set_outcome: Any debt balance history is reconstructed entirely from liability-account entries and reconciliation adjustments, with no field anywhere holding an authoritative cached balance.
items.set_parallel_boundary: Android and web can start against the published DebtType, RateConvention and StatementSnapshot schema as soon as the contracts package tags a version; neither client may reimplement flat-rate to reducing-balance conversion, which stays server-side only.
add_scope: A DebtType and RateConvention schema published to the contracts package so android and web read the same closed enum rather than each defining their own string constants
A reconciliation-adjustment audit trail that records which statement snapshot produced each adjustment, queryable per debt without joining application logs
A validation layer rejecting a debt payload whose minimum-payment-as-percentage value has no floor amount, since a pure percentage on a near-zero balance produces an unpayable minimum
A migration guard that fails a deploy if any existing debt row still carries a directly writable balance column, closing the door on the pattern this ticket removes
add_definition_of_done: A CI contract test proves the published schema exposes only integer minor units and integer basis points for every debt and reconciliation field
A reconciliation adjustment created against a seeded discrepancy in a test environment appears as a new ledger entry with the prior entries unchanged

items.summary: The ingestion pipeline must be extensible to sources that do not exist yet, because email, receipts, cash and any aggregator work all plug into the same precedence and deduplication rules.
add_acceptance_criteria: Adding a capture source requires registering it rather than changing the existing message and notification paths
Source precedence is data-driven so a new source can be positioned without a code change to existing sources
The pipeline rejects any payload containing raw message content at the boundary, enforced by the contract
Confidence is recorded per record on a defined scale with documented thresholds
add_contracts_schema: Consume T-CON-15's JSON Schemas for SourceEvent, TransactionCandidate, dedup decision and transaction provenance rather than publishing competing shapes in the API repository.
Version the pipeline contract with a schema_version field so android and api can evolve the candidate shape without breaking already-shipped parsers.
Add a contract test fixture set shared between api and android that both sides run in CI against the same golden payloads.
add_security_privacy: Enforce the raw-content-never-leaves-device boundary with a schema-level rejection: any payload field resembling raw message text is rejected at the contract boundary, not merely by convention.
Threat-model spoofed or malformed RawFinancialEvent payloads arriving from a compromised or reverse-engineered client and document the rejection behaviour.
Log a redacted audit trail per rejected payload, reason code only and no content, so repeated rejection attempts are detectable without retaining raw content.
add_observability: Emit a per-source dashboard panel showing parse-to-transaction conversion rate over rolling seven-day windows, so a silent drop in one channel is visible before users notice missing transactions.
Alert when any source's failed-event rate exceeds a defined threshold for more than one hour, paging the on-call owner named in docs#22.
Correlate pipeline stage logs with a single trace id per raw event so a stuck or dropped event can be traced end to end without inspecting raw content.
add_tests: New source registration test using a fixture source
Boundary test proving a raw content payload is rejected

Contract conformance test that fails the build when a candidate payload contains a field longer than the structured-field maximum, proving the raw-content boundary is enforced in code, not only in review.
Backward-compatibility test that replays a schema_version N candidate against the schema_version N+1 pipeline and confirms no data loss.
Load test that replays a realistic multi-source daily volume and confirms per-source metrics remain accurate under concurrent writes.
add_rollout_rollback: Roll out the source registry behind a flag per source, so a newly registered source can be disabled centrally without redeploying the pipeline core if it misbehaves.
Define a rollback path that reverts a pipeline schema_version bump without losing already-ingested candidates, verified by a rehearsal before the first schema change ships.
add_non_goals: Implementing Account Aggregator as a source; the enum reserves AA but this ticket does not build it.
Building the per-source parsers themselves; this ticket owns only the shared pipeline and registry, not android#7 or future EMAIL parsing.

replace_text.old: Publish a JSON schema for RawFinancialEvent, Candidate and Transaction that android#7, android#12 and api#18 all import rather than re-deriving field shapes independently.
replace_text.new: Consume T-CON-15's JSON Schemas for SourceEvent, TransactionCandidate, dedup decision and transaction provenance rather than publishing competing shapes in the API repository.

replace_text.old: Publish a versioned RawFinancialEvent-to-Transaction pipeline contract document listing every stage boundary (parse, candidate, dedupe, enrich) and the fields crossing it.
replace_text.new: Document the API implementation mapping from T-CON-15's SourceEvent and TransactionCandidate contracts through dedupe, enrichment and persisted provenance, without redefining contract-owned fields.

replace_text.new: T-CON-15 is pinned and its fixtures pass in at least one Android source (android#7 or android#12), this pipeline and api#18 before this ticket closes.

items.set_outcome: A new capture source is registered and flowing to Transaction records within one engineering day, with zero code changes to dedupe, enrich, or storage, and a reviewer signs off on that isolation.
items.set_parallel_boundary: api#18 dedupe work can start against the pinned T-CON-15 provenance fixtures before android#7's Kotlin parser is complete; the two converge only at the shared contract test suite, not at each other's code review.
add_scope: Document the API implementation mapping from T-CON-15's SourceEvent and TransactionCandidate contracts through dedupe, enrichment and persisted provenance, without redefining contract-owned fields.
Implement a source registry that other repositories consume to add MANUAL, SMS, NOTIFICATION, IMPORT, EMAIL and future sources without touching pipeline core code.
Wire the already-specified per-source metrics into a cross-repo dashboard reviewed weekly by android and api owners, closing the gap between counting failures and someone noticing them.
Define the confidence scale and needs_review threshold as a single shared constant consumed by every parser and the clarification inbox.
add_definition_of_done: T-CON-15 is pinned and its fixtures pass in at least one Android source (android#7 or android#12), this pipeline and api#18 before this ticket closes.
The per-source metrics dashboard is live and reviewed by an engineer outside the pipeline author's team.

items.summary: Offline persistence and the sync queue must be built against the published sync contract rather than an assumed server, which does not currently exist.
add_acceptance_criteria: The queue implements the published cursor and apply semantics rather than a locally invented protocol
A captured transaction survives process death, device restart and an application update
Replaying a queued change produces exactly one server effect
A poison record is isolated after the retry limit without blocking the rest of the queue
Every queued ingestion mutation carries the T-CON-15 source_event_id and source metadata unchanged across process death, retries and conflict resolution
add_contracts_schema: The mutation queue's wire payload for each entry matches the published cursor-and-apply schema exactly, including the idempotency key field name and type, with no locally renamed field
add_security_privacy: Idempotency keys are generated using a cryptographically random source, not a predictable counter, so a queue entry's key cannot be guessed or replayed by another process on a shared device
add_observability: Queue depth, oldest-pending-entry age and poison-record count are each exposed as client metrics, so a systemic sync problem across many devices is visible in aggregate rather than only per-device
add_tests: Durability test across process death and restart
Duplicate apply test
A 48-hour simulated offline test accumulates a realistic volume of mutations, then reconnects and asserts the queue drains completely with the correct final sync status
A concurrency test issues two devices' worth of mutations against the same account and asserts the poison-isolation path does not block unrelated entries from either device
add_rollout_rollback: The queue's on-disk schema version is checked at app startup; an app rollback that predates a queue schema change reads and drains the old-format queue instead of discarding it
add_non_goals: Resolving a genuine conflicting edit between two devices; the stated last-writer-wins policy on metadata is out of scope for enhancement in this ticket
Syncing data types other than debts, transactions and accounts; other future entity types are not covered by this queue implementation
Nothing in this ticket changed with the move from Sprint 08 to Sprint 09; the move creates room for the shared privacy contract T-CON-09, which the trust and compliance surfaces all consume
items.set_outcome: Force-killing the app mid-sync, rebooting the device, and reconnecting after 48 hours offline replays every queued mutation exactly once, with the sync status indicator showing synced only after the server has acknowledged the last entry.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket cannot begin integration against a real server until the sync contract publishes its cursor-and-apply schema; local queue persistence and the debug inspection screen can be built against a mocked contract in parallel.
add_scope: A queue-depth cap with a documented user-facing message when exceeded, so a user offline for an extended period sees an honest too-many-pending-changes state rather than an unbounded, silently growing queue
A manual retry-now action for a failed mutation, distinct from the automatic backoff, so a user is not stuck waiting for the next scheduled retry window after fixing their connection
A queue-inspection debug screen (developer-only build variant) listing pending, failed and poison entries with their idempotency keys, to support field diagnosis without querying the raw database
add_definition_of_done: The 48-hour offline drain test passes with the queue fully drained and the sync status indicator showing synced only at true completion
The queue-depth cap and its user-facing message have been reviewed for tone against the same honesty standard applied to the never-payoff case

items.summary: The message permission ticket must cover the states that follow the grant, which is where the real user experience problems are, and it must be verified on a physical device against the golden corpus.
add_acceptance_criteria: Post-grant revocation from system settings leaves the application in a clear, recoverable state rather than failing silently
A recovery path guides the user back to granting the permission, or to manual entry, without dead ends
The restricted settings path is verified on a physical device rather than an emulator
The declaration content matches the captured traffic evidence rather than the code's intent
The permission rationale screen is screen-reader traversable and usable at the largest text scale
The declaration is filed against a build produced by the T-REL-01 release pipeline and published to a real track, so the submitted artifact is the artifact the pipeline signs
add_contracts_schema: Publish the permission-state contract (granted, denied, revoked, never-asked) consumed consistently by onboarding, the recovery path and android#10's notification equivalent, so the two permission flows do not diverge in behaviour.
add_security_privacy: Confirm the network-inspection evidence used for the Play declaration is captured on a build identical to what ships, not a debug build with different behaviour, so the evidence is not misleading.
Document the contingency path in writing: if the declaration is rejected, manual entry and import remain fully functional and no feature is silently disabled without user-visible explanation.
add_observability: Instrument the onboarding funnel (dialog shown, granted, denied, recovered) so the real denial and recovery rate is measured rather than assumed, matching the approach android#10 already applies to notification access.
Alert if the post-grant revocation recovery path's completion rate drops sharply after an OS update, since Android permission behaviour changes between versions without notice.
add_tests: Physical device revocation and recovery test
Traffic capture assertion that no raw message content leaves the device
Screen-reader traversal test for the permission rationale screen at the largest supported text scale, run on a physical device.
Rejection-contingency test: with permission denied throughout, exercise the full manual-entry and import flow end to end and confirm no feature is blocked.
add_rollout_rollback: Submit the Play Permissions Declaration during the beta window as planned, with a documented fallback timeline of manual and notification channels only if the review or an appeal is not resolved before the intended launch date.
add_non_goals: Building the notification-access equivalent onboarding; that flow is owned by android#10 and follows a different OS mechanism.
Redesigning the manual-entry flow itself; this ticket verifies it remains usable when permission is denied, it does not change its implementation.
items.set_outcome: A user who denies SMS permission can still add, categorise and track a transaction manually, and network inspection during the Play review window confirms zero raw SMS bytes leave the device.
items.set_parallel_boundary: The onboarding UI and recovery-path design can be built and reviewed before android#7 and android#8 are feature-complete, since the declaration and network-inspection evidence require only a working permission dialog and a stub parser; full traffic-inspection evidence is gated on a build that includes the real parser.
add_scope: Design the single unobtrusive re-consideration path for a user who denied permission, distinct from the initial onboarding explanation, so denial is not silently permanent nor aggressively re-prompted.
Prepare the demo video and reviewer test credentials required by the Play Permissions Declaration Form as concrete, checked-in deliverables rather than a submission-day task.
Verify store listing copy against the current policy wording before submission, since the declaration can be rejected on marketing-copy grounds alone.
add_definition_of_done: The onboarding funnel metrics (shown, granted, denied, recovered) are instrumented and reviewed before the declaration is submitted.
The rejection-contingency test passes and its evidence is attached to the declaration submission record.

items.summary: The clarification inbox needs the conflict and rollback experiences it currently lacks, and it must be accessible, because it is the screen where a user corrects the application's mistakes.
add_acceptance_criteria: A deduplication conflict is presented with both candidates and the reason one was preferred, and the user can choose
A rule created from a clarification can be rolled back, and the rollback states what it will change
Clarifications are batched so the user is never repeatedly interrupted for the same item
Every inbox surface is screen-reader traversable and usable at the largest text scale
Resolving a clarification offline queues correctly and converges without duplicating the resolution
add_contracts_schema: Consume api#18's merge-decision schema directly for the conflict-presentation surface, rather than re-deriving a simplified view of it that could drift from the real precedence logic.
Consume api#19's merchant-rule schema for the rollback surface so the same rule representation is shown and edited consistently.
add_security_privacy: Confirm the conflict-presentation surface displays only structured candidate fields, amount, merchant, timestamp, never any raw message text that may exist upstream of the pipeline boundary.
Scope offline-queued resolutions to the authenticated account so a device-level queue cannot leak or apply to the wrong account after a sign-out and sign-in.
add_observability: Instrument conflict-resolution outcomes, which candidate chosen and how often the suggested one is overridden, separately from the existing low-confidence resolution metrics, since a high override rate signals the precedence logic itself needs review.
Track rollback usage rate; a rising rate indicates rules are being created incorrectly and the correction flow needs review.
add_tests: Conflict presentation test
Rule rollback test
Accessibility traversal test
Offline-resolution convergence test: resolve the same clarification twice from two queued devices and confirm only one resolution applies.
Rollback correctness test: create a rule from a clarification, roll it back, and confirm the prior categorisation state is restored exactly.
add_rollout_rollback: Ship the conflict-presentation and rollback surfaces to a small cohort first and compare override and rollback rates against the existing categorisation-only flow before full rollout.
add_non_goals: Changing the underlying dedupe precedence rules; this ticket only presents api#18's decisions and lets the user see the reasoning, it does not alter the merge engine.
Building a general rule-management screen; the rollback surface here is scoped to clarification-originated rules only.
items.set_outcome: Fifty seeded unknown transactions are cleared by a real user at a median under five seconds each, and a resolved merchant is confirmed never to reappear in a later batch.
items.set_parallel_boundary: The clarification list UI and batching logic can be built against synthetic low-confidence fixtures independent of api#18 and api#19 landing; the conflict-presentation and rollback surfaces are gated on those two tickets' schemas being published, not on their full production rollout.
add_scope: Design the conflict-presentation UI that shows both deduplication candidates and the reason one was preferred, as distinct from the existing low-confidence categorisation review flow.
Build the rollback surface for a rule created from a clarification, stating in plain language what will change before the user confirms.
Implement offline queuing for clarification resolutions with a convergence rule that prevents a duplicate resolution when connectivity returns.
add_definition_of_done: The conflict-presentation and rollback surfaces are timed with a real user alongside the existing five-second median requirement, not assumed to meet it by design.
The offline-resolution convergence test passes and is added to the permanent regression suite.

items.summary: Continuous integration cannot honestly require language-specific build, test and lint until the repositories contain something to build. This ticket becomes the conformance gate over the reusable workflows and the six scaffolds; branch protection wiring is not its work, because T-SCA-INF-01 solely owns it.
items.set_title: Enforce CI conformance across the eight repositories
add_acceptance_criteria: Every repository consumes the reusable workflow published by T-SCA-INF-01 rather than a locally copied pipeline
The conformance job runs against the delivered scaffolds and fails when a build, test or lint step is stubbed or removed
Required check names are standardised by T-SCA-INF-01, and this gate fails when a repository declares a required check name that no workflow actually produces
Branch protection wiring is owned solely by T-SCA-INF-01 and is out of scope here; this gate verifies only that the standardised checks exist, run and can fail
Third-party actions are pinned by commit rather than by moving tag
The gate is evidenced by a planted-defect run per language, not by inspection of workflow files
remove_acceptance_criteria: Each repo has a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on PR and on push to `main`
add_contracts_schema: A JSON schema for the required-check-name registry (repo, check_name, workflow_ref, language) consumed directly by the T-SCA-INF-01 branch protection automation.
add_security_privacy: The conformance workflow runs with read-only permissions and no repository secrets, since it only inspects check results and workflow run metadata.
add_observability: A published per-repository CI wall-clock trend so a regression toward the existing 10 minute budget triggers an alert before it becomes tolerated as normal.
add_tests: Conformance job self-test with a fixture repository containing a stubbed test step
Registry-schema test that rejects a check-name registry entry missing a required field, run before the entry can reach the branch protection automation.
add_rollout_rollback: Roll out the conformance gate as non-blocking report-only per repository before flipping it to required, and roll back a single repository to its prior workflow reference if the reusable workflow regresses across multiple repositories at once.
add_non_goals: Authoring the language-specific build, test and lint steps themselves, which remain owned by each repository's own scaffold ticket.
