items.summary: Financial account management sits in the accounts and manual-entry wave of the replanned baseline. Its Sprint and Status are stated here so the field value is authoritative rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan.
add_contracts_schema: An account resource schema (id, name, type, currency, institution, masked_number, archived_at_or_null) published once so contracts#1 and this ticket cannot diverge on field names or types.
add_security_privacy: A full account number received during account creation is never persisted or logged beyond the last-4 mask, verified by inspecting the request-handling code path rather than only the stored schema.
add_observability: A count of archive attempts blocked because they targeted an account with existing entries, exposed as a metric so an unexpectedly high rate signals a client-side bug attempting hard deletes.
add_tests: Currency-registry validation test asserting account creation is rejected for a currency code absent from the exponent registry.
add_rollout_rollback: Ship account management behind a feature flag scoped to internal test accounts first, and roll back by disabling the flag if the computed-balance-on-read query proves too slow under a realistic account and entry volume, before it reaches any real user.
add_non_goals: Supporting joint or shared accounts across multiple users, which is not part of the account model this ticket defines.
items.set_outcome: Attempting to hard-delete an account that has at least one ledger entry is rejected by the application layer with an error naming the archive alternative, rather than succeeding silently or throwing a generic database error.
items.set_context: Accounts are the ledger boundary users understand: bank accounts, cards, cash and debts. Their identifiers, currency and archive semantics are consumed by transaction creation, import, sync and every client, so this ticket must publish one stable resource shape and preserve history rather than behaving like ordinary mutable CRUD.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns account CRUD and its ledger-facing invariants inside the api repository; the android, web and admin repositories consume the published account resource schema and define no account field set of their own.
add_scope: An account-listing endpoint that separates active from archived accounts by default, so archived accounts do not silently reappear in a client that forgot to filter.
A validation rule rejecting an account creation request whose currency code is absent from the currency-exponent registry introduced by api#1.
A masked-number formatting function shared with the import ticket api#10, so both paths mask account numbers identically.
add_definition_of_done: A reviewer attempts to hard-delete an account with at least one entry through the actual API surface, not a direct database call, and confirms it is rejected with the archive-alternative error.

items.summary: Own-account transfers sit in the accounts and manual-entry wave and cannot start before the transaction write path exists. Its Sprint and Status are stated here so the field value is authoritative rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan.
add_contracts_schema: A transfer-pair schema (from_account_id, to_account_id, fx_rate_or_null, rate_captured_at) distinct from the general transaction schema, since a transfer always references exactly two accounts and no category.
add_security_privacy: No new security or privacy control is introduced by this ticket beyond those already enforced on the underlying transaction and account records, since a transfer carries no additional sensitive field.
add_observability: A count of transactions edited from transfer to a spending category or back after creation, alerting if the rate is nonzero given the validation rule meant to prevent it.
add_tests: Re-categorisation guard test asserting an attempt to change a transfer's category through the general edit endpoint is rejected.

items.set_outcome: A report generated for a period before and after a stored FX rate is later corrected still shows the originally recorded rate in the historical report, proving the rate is genuinely immutable once attached to a transaction.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket owns transfer semantics and the FX-rate-at-transaction-date rule inside the api repository; the automated-capture epic, tracked separately, consumes this ticket's candidate-pair flag rather than redefining transfer detection.
add_scope: A transfer-detection heuristic threshold specification, amount and date proximity, distinct from the automated-capture epic's own matching logic, so this ticket states what counts as a candidate pair without implementing the capture pipeline.

A validation rule preventing a transfer from being re-categorised into an income or expense category through the general transaction-edit path, since that would silently break the transfer exclusion guarantee.
A reconciliation report comparing total transfers recorded against total transfers excluded from income and expense sums, to catch a future regression where a transfer leaks into a totals query.

items.summary: The amortisation engine sits in the deterministic debt wave, after the debt model and before every projection that reads it. Its Sprint and Status are stated here so the field value is authoritative rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan.
add_contracts_schema: AmortisationResult schema is a tagged union (Schedule or NeverPayoff), so the generated client gets an exhaustive branch rather than a nullable payoff date
Each schedule period entry publishes principal, interest, fees and closing balance as MinorUnitAmount, reusing the same named schema type as the debt model rather than a locally redefined shape
add_security_privacy: Cached amortisation schedules are keyed by an input hash rather than a user-visible identifier, so a cache key alone cannot be used to enumerate another user's debt figures
Schedule computation logs the input hash and period count only, never the principal, rate or balance values, at any log level
add_observability: A histogram tracks amortisation computation latency per period count, so a regression toward the 30-year, 20-debt budget is visible before users notice slower simulations
The never-payoff detection path emits its own counter, separate from normal payoff completions, so a sudden shift in that ratio after a deploy is visible
add_tests: A CI gate re-runs the independent-model comparison on every change touching debt or amortisation code and blocks the merge on any paisa-level mismatch
A determinism test computes the same schedule twice in the same process and twice across separate process invocations, asserting all four results are identical
add_rollout_rollback: The engine ships as an internal library with no public endpoint of its own in this ticket; a rollback simply reverts the library version consumed by the projection service
A schedule-format version tag accompanies every cached result so a rollback that changes rounding behaviour cannot be served a stale schedule computed under the old rule
add_non_goals: Exposing the amortisation engine as its own externally callable endpoint; it is consumed only by the projection service in this phase
Supporting mid-term interest rate changes driven by an external rate feed; only an explicitly supplied rate change is in scope
items.set_outcome: Given identical debt inputs on any date, the engine returns byte-identical periodic schedules and total interest figures across ten repeated runs, with the never-payoff case returned as a typed result rather than a runaway loop.
items.set_parallel_boundary: The engine and its independent reference dataset can be built in parallel by different contributors once the interest-accrual convention constant is agreed; the projection service must not start consuming the engine until the AmortisationResult schema is published.
add_scope: A typed AmortisationResult union distinguishing a normal payoff schedule from a NeverPayoff result, published through contracts so no client has to infer the difference from a null date
A schedule-length guard that returns a typed error rather than computing an unbounded number of periods when a malformed rate would otherwise loop indefinitely
A documented interest-accrual convention recorded as a single named constant that the engine and its independent reference both cite
A performance budget test harness that runs the 360-period, 20-debt case and fails the build if wall-clock time regresses past the stated threshold
add_definition_of_done: The independent-model comparison runs in CI on every relevant change and has blocked at least one deliberately introduced paisa-level defect during review
The never-payoff result type is consumed by at least one caller in a way that is exercised by a test, proving it is not a theoretical case

items.summary: Portfolio payoff projection sits in the deterministic debt wave and reads the amortisation engine rather than caching its own balances. Its Sprint and Status are stated here so the field value is authoritative rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan.
add_contracts_schema: PortfolioProjection schema publishes a discriminated result: OnTrack with a debt-free date, or NotOnTrack with the shortfall amount, so clients cannot mistake one for the other
Progress fields (percentagePaid, principalCleared, interestPaidToDate) are published as named schema types shared with the debt entity rather than re-derived client-side
add_security_privacy: Cached projection entries are evicted when the owning account is deleted, so a projection hash cannot outlive the debt data it was computed from
add_observability: A metric records the fraction of portfolios currently in the NotOnTrack state only above a minimum aggregation threshold and with no per-user identifier
Cache hit and miss rates for the projection cache are tracked so an invalidation bug that recomputes every request is visible as a hit-rate drop
add_tests: A cache invalidation test changes one debt in a five-debt portfolio and asserts the recomputed projection differs only in the fields that debt affects
A load test issues the 20-debt, 30-year projection repeatedly and asserts the 100ms budget holds under concurrent requests, not only in isolation
add_rollout_rollback: The projection cache can be flushed independently of a code rollback, so a rollback that changes rounding behaviour is never served a projection computed under the prior rule
add_non_goals: Any AI-generated narration of the projection; this ticket returns numbers only, narration is out of scope per the no-LLM rule already stated
Projections for hypothetical debts not yet saved; that capability belongs to the simulator ticket
items.set_outcome: Given a fixed portfolio of debts, the portfolio-wide debt-free date, total interest remaining and progress percentages are identical across repeated calls and match an independently built reference to the day.
items.set_parallel_boundary: This ticket can proceed in parallel with the countdown screen work once the PortfolioProjection schema is published; the countdown screen may render placeholder data against the schema before the projection service's cache tuning is finished.
add_scope: A projection cache invalidation rule keyed on a hash of every input debt and its payment history, so a single changed debt cannot leave stale figures visible for the others
A published NotOnTrack result type distinct from a normal projection, carrying the shortfall amount between minimum payment and accruing interest
A roll-forward audit field recording which debt absorbed a cleared debt's payment for each period, so the ordering is inspectable rather than only asserted by test
add_definition_of_done: The cache invalidation rule is exercised by a test that would fail if a changed debt left a stale sibling projection
The NotOnTrack shortfall figure has been verified against the same independent reference used for the amortisation engine

items.summary: Strategy comparison sits in the deterministic debt wave and is the surface the Android comparison screen consumes. Its Sprint and Status are stated here so the field value is authoritative rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan.

CustomOrder request schema is a list of debt identifiers with a minItems and uniqueItems constraint enforced by the schema itself, not only by server-side validation
add_security_privacy: Strategy comparison responses carry no field identifying a specific lender or account beyond the debt identifiers already visible to the requesting user
add_observability: A metric records which strategy (avalanche, snowball or custom) is most frequently viewed last in a session, informing whether the snowball motivation framing is being used as intended
The tie-break path emits a counter distinct from the normal ordering path, so an unexpectedly high tie rate after a data change is visible
add_tests: A determinism test runs the same comparison one hundred times across separate process starts and asserts the tie-break ordering never varies
A property test asserts total principal repaid is identical across avalanche, snowball, hybrid and custom orderings for the same portfolio, since only the order, not the total, should change
Hybrid strategy transition tests cover every documented threshold and tie-break boundary.
add_rollout_rollback: The comparison-result cache is versioned separately from the projection cache so a rollback of comparison logic alone does not require invalidating unrelated projection caches
add_non_goals: Recommending a single strategy to the user; this ticket returns a comparison only, per the advice-boundary rule already stated
Persisting a user's chosen strategy as an instruction to automatically reorder future payments; strategy selection is display-only in this ticket

items.set_parallel_boundary: The Android comparison screen can be built against the StrategyComparison schema stub before this ticket's cache tuning lands, provided the client never recomputes interest or time saved itself.
add_scope: A documented, published tie-break rule (for example, lowest debt identifier wins an equal-APR or equal-balance tie) so results are reproducible across servers and not an artifact of map iteration order
A CustomOrder validation step rejecting an ordering that omits or duplicates a debt, returning a typed error rather than silently reordering
A comparison-result cache keyed on portfolio hash and strategy name, separate from the single-strategy projection cache, so comparing strategies does not multiply projection cost
A hybrid strategy whose debt ordering rule and transition criteria are explicit and deterministic rather than a marketing label.
add_definition_of_done: The published tie-break rule is exercised by a dedicated test fixture containing at least one genuine tie
The principal-invariance property test passes for every strategy on the same fixture portfolio

items.summary: The extra-payment simulator sits in the deterministic debt wave alongside strategy comparison. Its Sprint and Status are stated here so the field value is authoritative rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan.

SimulationResult schema explicitly marks itself as ephemeral (not persisted) in its description, so a generated client does not treat it as a cacheable resource with an identifier

add_observability: A metric tracks binary-search iteration counts for the inverse query, so a change to convergence behaviour that silently increases latency is visible before the 100ms budget is breached
A counter distinguishes simulations that returned an honest 'target unreachable' result from ones that returned a date, so the unreachable-target rate is visible over time

A test verifies the inverse query's binary search terminates within its documented iteration cap on a portfolio engineered to be barely payable
add_rollout_rollback: The simulator's read-only connection pool can be rolled back independently of the projection service, since a regression here cannot corrupt stored data by construction
add_non_goals: Saving a simulated extra-payment amount as the user's actual payment plan; committing a plan is a separate, explicit action outside this ticket
Simulating a strategy change together with an extra payment in a single request; this ticket simulates payment amount only
items.set_outcome: Dragging a simulated extra-payment value from zero back to zero returns exactly the stored baseline projection, and every intermediate value returns a result within the 100ms budget without writing to any stored debt.
items.set_parallel_boundary: The Android simulator slider can be developed against the SimulationRequest and SimulationResult schema before this ticket's binary-search tuning is finalised, since the contract shape, not the convergence speed, is what the client depends on.
add_scope: A read-only simulation boundary enforced at the data-access layer, not only by convention, so a future change to the simulator cannot accidentally acquire a write connection
A bounded binary search for the inverse target-date query with an explicit iteration cap and a documented closest-achievable fallback response
A 'pay off debt X today' request validated against the requesting user's own portfolio so it cannot be pointed at a debt identifier belonging to another account
add_definition_of_done: The read-only enforcement test passes, demonstrating a write attempt from simulation code fails rather than succeeding silently
The binary-search iteration cap test passes on a portfolio deliberately constructed to be at the edge of payability

items.summary: The independent verification suite closes the deterministic debt wave and is what makes the debt numbers defensible rather than merely tested against themselves. add_contracts_schema: The reference dataset is stored as a schema-validated fixture file (debt inputs plus expected schedule) so a malformed fixture fails fast rather than silently comparing against garbage
add_security_privacy: Reference scenarios use synthetic debt figures rather than any real user's data, so the committed fixture file carries no privacy exposure
add_observability: The CI job reports, per run, how many of the mutation-testing injected errors were caught, so a regression in the suite's own sensitivity is visible as a falling catch count over time
add_tests: A meta-test asserts the mutation-testing harness itself injects at least one error per code path it claims to cover, so an uncovered path cannot silently pass by omission
A scenario is added covering a flat-rate BNPL loan specifically, since the live scenario list does not name this combination explicitly
add_rollout_rollback: The verification suite is additive to CI and blocks merges rather than deployments, so there is no runtime rollback path; a failing suite is resolved by fixing the code or, with review, correcting a documented reference error
add_non_goals: Verifying the Android or web client's own rendering of these figures; this suite verifies the API's computed values only
Building a general-purpose fuzzing framework; the mutation catalogue here is fixed and curated for the debt-math domain

items.set_parallel_boundary: The reference-dataset provenance work can proceed independently of the amortisation, projection, strategy and simulator tickets once their output schemas are frozen; the mutation-testing harness must wait until the engine's public entry points are stable, since it targets those entry points directly.
add_scope: A reference-dataset provenance file recording, per scenario, which external tool or library produced the expected schedule and its version, so a future mismatch can be diagnosed as a code regression or a stale reference
A mutation-testing harness that programmatically injects a fixed catalogue of small numeric errors into the engine and asserts the suite fails on each one
A scenario-coverage report listing which debt type, rate convention and edge case each of the twenty-plus scenarios exercises, so a gap is visible rather than assumed covered
add_definition_of_done: The mutation-testing harness demonstrates a 100 percent catch rate against its own fixed error catalogue in the most recent CI run
The scenario-coverage report shows no debt type or rate convention combination named in the debt-modelling ticket without at least one covering scenario

items.summary: Cross-channel deduplication sits in the ingestion automation wave and depends on the ingestion pipeline it filters. Its Sprint and Status are stated here so the field value is authoritative rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan.
add_acceptance_criteria: Confidence is reported using the shared confidence band component from T-CON-10 and the categorisation confidence shape from T-CON-02; this ticket publishes no third confidence encoding

add_contracts_schema: Consume and, when required through contract-first change, extend T-CON-15's dedup-decision record (candidate ids, matched fields, precedence winner, timestamp) for the clarification inbox in android#11.

Treat a burst of near-identical candidates from a single source as a potential replay or spoofed-input signal and flag it for review rather than merging silently.

Alert when the merge rate for any single merchant spikes abnormally, since that pattern historically indicates a broken source feed rather than genuine duplicate payments.

Regression test pinning every historical false-merge or false-split incident as a permanent adversarial case, mirroring the golden-corpus pattern used for parsers.
add_rollout_rollback: Ship the merge engine behind a beta-cohort shadow mode that records privacy-safe aggregate decisions without applying them, so false merges are measured before enforcement.
Provide a rollback that reverts a bad precedence-table change to the prior version without needing to reprocess already-merged records.

Deduplicating statement-import batches against each other on ingestion order; only cross-source duplicates are in scope here.

items.set_parallel_boundary: The merge engine and its audit-record schema can be built and unit-tested against synthetic fixtures while android#7's parser is still in progress; only the shadow-mode rollout against real traffic is gated on android#7 and android#12 shipping real candidates.
add_scope: Implement the fuzzy match and merge decision engine as a standalone, independently testable module callable by both live capture and statement import.
Build a merge-audit record that stores which two candidates merged, which fields each contributed, and which precedence rule decided the winner.
Expose a manual unmerge action so a false-merge caught late can be reversed without a database migration.

The merge-audit schema is confirmed consumed by android#11 before this ticket closes, not left as an unused contract.

items.summary: Merchant normalisation, categorisation rules and recurring detection sit in the ingestion automation wave. Its Sprint and Status are stated here so the field value is authoritative rather than inherited from the superseded delivery plan.
add_contracts_schema: Publish the merchant-rule schema (pattern, canonical name, category, created_by_user flag) as a versioned contract so a future rule-editing UI can read and write it without api internals leaking through.
Define the recurring-item schema (merchant, interval, amount range, monthly total) as a stable contract for the subscription list surface.
add_security_privacy: Ensure user-created categorisation rules are scoped to the owning account and never leak across tenants during rule lookup or the recurring-detection scan.
Confirm the deterministic-only constraint is enforced at the boundary: no external model or network call is reachable from this code path, keeping the E18 AI baseline comparison honest.
add_observability: Track normalisation-miss rate (transactions that fail to resolve to a canonical merchant) as a first-class metric, since a rising miss rate signals the merchant corpus needs expansion before users notice repeat prompts.
Instrument how often a user re-corrects a merchant already covered by an existing rule, which indicates a rule-matching bug rather than a genuinely new merchant.
add_tests: Regression test that a rule created from one correction is applied to every future transaction from the same normalised merchant without re-prompting, run against a sanitized synthetic Indian merchant corpus.
Boundary test proving the categorisation path makes no network call, so the deterministic-only requirement is enforced in code rather than by policy.
add_rollout_rollback: Ship recurring detection to a subset of accounts first and compare detected subscription totals against manually reviewed accounts before enabling it broadly.
Provide a way to disable a single misbehaving user rule centrally without deleting the user's other rules, in case a rule conflict causes miscategorisation at scale.
add_non_goals: AI-assisted categorisation; this ticket's baseline exists specifically so E18 has a deterministic bar to beat, and does not implement any model inference itself.
Editing rules from a web or admin surface; this ticket owns the engine and storage, not a rule-management UI.
items.set_outcome: A user who corrects one Swiggy transaction's category is never asked about a Swiggy transaction again, and the subscription list surfaces a correct total monthly cost across a seeded six-month corpus.
items.set_context: Merchant normalisation and deterministic categorisation turn captured transactions into a useful product without sending financial text to a model. items.set_parallel_boundary: Merchant normalisation and the rule engine can be developed against api#18's merge-audit fixtures without waiting for api#18 to reach production; recurring detection additionally needs at least six months of seeded or replayed transaction history before its accuracy can be judged.
add_scope: Build the merchant normalisation table as data (raw-pattern to canonical-name mapping) that can be extended without a code deploy, mirroring the remote-rule approach used for android#8's parser config.
Implement the rule engine's conflict resolution for two rules that could both match the same normalised merchant, with a deterministic tie-break documented.
Ship the recurring-detection window and tolerance (amount variation, date drift) as named, reviewable constants rather than implicit code.
add_definition_of_done: The normalisation-miss rate is measured against a sanitized synthetic Indian merchant corpus and recorded alongside the baseline categorisation accuracy already required.
A reviewer confirms no network call is reachable from the categorisation or recurring-detection code path.

Confirm the remote-config fetch itself carries no user data beyond what is strictly needed to select the correct rule set, so the update channel does not become a privacy leak.
add_observability: Alert when per-sender parse-success telemetry drops below a defined threshold for any bank sender, distinct from simply collecting the telemetry.
Track rule-set fetch failures and stale-cache duration per device cohort, so a broken distribution path is caught before it silently degrades parsing for weeks.
add_tests: Signature-rotation test: a device holding a rule set signed by the outgoing key still validates correctly during a key rotation window, without a gap in trusted parsing.
Sandbox-escape negative test: a deliberately malicious rule payload attempting excessive resource use or a malformed regex is contained without affecting other app functions.
add_rollout_rollback: Stage a new rule set to a small device cohort and compare its parse-success telemetry against the prior rule set before promoting it to all devices.
Rehearse the safe-rollback path on a schedule, not only when something breaks, so the mechanism is proven working before it is needed under pressure.
add_non_goals: Building the golden-corpus test suite itself; this ticket consumes android#7's fixtures to validate new rule sets, it does not define new test content.
Supporting arbitrary code execution in rules; rules remain declarative data, and any capability requiring code is out of scope.
items.set_outcome: A deliberately broken parser rule is corrected and re-deployed to a test device within the sync schedule, with no app release, and tampered-payload rejection is demonstrated in the same rehearsal.
items.set_parallel_boundary: The signing, sandboxing and fetch-schedule mechanism can be built and tested against android#7's bundled rule format before android#7's Kotlin parser fully lands; convergence happens only when the first real remote rule update is pushed against a shipped parser.
add_scope: Define the signing and version-check mechanism for rule payloads, including which key signs them and how the app verifies the signature before caching a new rule set.
Build the sandbox boundary that isolates rule evaluation from the rest of the app so a malformed rule cannot crash or hang the parsing pipeline.
Implement the safe-rollback path as a specific, tested action, revert to the prior signed version, rather than an assumed capability.
add_definition_of_done: A key-rotation rehearsal is demonstrated without a gap in trusted parsing, alongside the already-required break-and-fix cycle.
The sandbox-escape negative test passes and is added to the permanent regression suite.
